newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Trans Hex sees further growth for full yr.
newsitem.headline: Trans Hex sees further growth for full yr.

text.p: South Africa's Trans Hex Group Ltd said on Tuesday it is confident that its diamond division will continue to maintain its operational performance and its lime division will increase its contribution to profits.

"The pressure on prices of lower quality diamonds is expected to continue, however better quality gem diamond, which comprise the bulk of the group's production, will remain in high demand," the firm said in a statement with its half year results.
"In addition, the lime division is expected to improve its contribution to the bottom line," Trans Hex added.

Trans Hex, which mines and sells rough diamonds as well as dolomite and limestones, posted earnings per share up 180 cents from 133.5 cents previously. The dividend was increased to 40.0 cents from 34.0 cents last time.
The group said production and sales in the lime division were on schedule and the new calcining facility at Vredendal had achieved further improvements in volumes and product quallity.
It recently transferred its foreign exploration interest to Canadian registered Trans Hex International Ltd.

Trans Hex International raised C$18 million in the period under review which would be used to further diamond exploration in the Central African Republic, Brazil, Indonesia and Namibia, the group said.
